argument:
JPMorgan's $16.9bn net income excluding significant items offers a better bullish anchor than the $21.2bn headline. Average loans grew 10% and deposits 7%, showing an active franchise under the observed resilient-demand backdrop. If credit costs and funding remain controlled, that larger operating base could sustain profitable banking activity through the current correction.

Visa/equity gains inflate headline EPS, credit costs reached $2.5bn, and CET1 and liquidity ratios have not been extracted. A Fed hike is not automatically a margin windfall because deposit repricing matters. Price above SMA-200 preserves some longer-term support, but below SMA-50 with negative MACD and RSI near 28 is not a reversal confirmation. The bull case requires bank-specific capital and credit validation.
key_points: Earnings excluding significant items remain substantial.
Loan and deposit growth support franchise activity.
Credit, funding and capital evidence must establish durability.
